### 免治港人 | 1983
### 堅持港人治港,
**免治港人**
*(我們現正朝著一個偉大的歷史目標前進,得到初步的成果,港英派已經作大轉鬆,要承認及接受政治現實,歷史的巨輪是不能抵抗的,我們要堅持港人治港,堅持中國在一九九年恢愎香港主權,堅持香港政制民立化,現況是值得鼓舞的,港英公開表示立法局會在不久將來舉行民選,我們要堅持到底,使香港可以邁向一個高度民主淆的社會。
在堅持民族之義和民主化的前提下,滙點、新香港學會....等的團體為香港五百萬居民,為廣大民家爭取利益,它們的貢獻正面的、有益的,有建設性的。《學苑》中一少撮文章都正在進行破壞這些堅持,一些作者「更立烈地打擊港人治港的信心,以為民主化不可行,向酒點的成員(方卡謬先生、艾凡先生一盧子健同學等)作無理及惡毒的批評和攻擊, 盲罵他們的意識形態,這類反面作者利用一些洋
奴理論去作假學術,實只是負面地作人格攻擊。
要知道艾凡先生在葡轄澳門有廠房投資,妻子為美國公民,還如虎似狼一般為港人治港盡力, 當上滙點的主席,又在某報副刊及一些雜誌撰文, 多次出席座談會和講座……他的犧牲自我的精神是值得我們效法的。方卡謬先生更從七十年代開始便好社會現象有尖銳的批判,他在《文化新潮》、《財經日報副刊的香江評論》及《號外 >>等有很多文章,讓我隨便抽些內容和大家分享:「岑逸飛食美國保飯,戴天借醉調戲文化八婆………龜頭之下無淨土,故此,戴天實在無需為自己的龜頭活動懊悔………」(文化新潮算7期p.27)、「錢瑪利小姐坦蕩湯之際,竟然毫無睇頭,兩隻乳房(IF IT IS THE RIGIT WORD)小得可憐,正一煎爛荷包蛋,乳頭則像肚池餅………成俊淫羊咁款,收到我脹。」 (文化新潮第八期 p.55)、張有與………不怪自己权才成性, 文化贩子作秀如此,無恥如此……同樣等而下之者,则是「香港前是社」一数酸秀 ….」.香江評論 31-1-84),總之都是方卡謬夠堅,大罵港英、 小資產階級的港獨、反對或不信「港人治港」者為過街老鼠」,貶格奴才」,他詞峰尖銳,對這些文化奴才走狗點名批鬥, 真是一流一流,拍按案叫绝! !他的人格是絕頂好的,不容《學苑》某小撮小人破壞。 
我希望每位堅持港人民主治港的同志向方卡學習,閱讀他在各報刊的無數作品。無論在思想和行為上,方卡謬先生真不愧為香港的新文化人! 唐老番說得好一方卡謬先生還比李敖勁!
除了滙點以外,黃夢花醫生也是很值得尊敬的,他身為加拿大籍人,但仍然努力不懈地為香港工作,放棄了只能引致政治自殺的「港獨」思想,投入我們的行列中,黃麗松技長更是我們應該學習的模範,他雖然是新加坡公民,但也非常關心香港前途問題,對推行港人治港不遺餘力,他們的行動都是有建做性、符合整個歷史政治環境的。
令人可喜的是許家屯先生也曾出席過港大的評議會及滙點一週年的會議,這點証明中國非常重視為今的知識份子。我們必定可以改變現狀,正如盧子健兄所說,大顯身手,一齊建設,為香港人爭取光榮。
我提議由上述的人才選出將來的市長,領導香港人進行民主改革,使我們的前途似錦,光明磊落,無愧於天!
歷史一次又一次證明,堅持港人治港和港民主化是香港的唯一出路,那些虛無主義個人主義者勢必失效。我們在這個歷史契機的基本任務和使命是為建設一個高度民主自治的香港,讓我們繼續完成這個基本責任,為中國的统一盡力。
### English Translation
_(preserving the essay's sarcastic register — this is satire, not sincere praise)_
**Uphold "Hong Kong People Ruling Hong Kong," Uphold the Democratization of Hong Kong's Political System — A Tribute to Meeting Point**
By Minced Hong Kong Person
We are now marching toward a great historic goal, and initial results are in: the pro-British-Hong-Kong faction has already made a great about-face, forced to acknowledge and accept political reality — the great wheel of history cannot be resisted. We must uphold "Hong Kong people ruling Hong Kong," uphold China's resumption of sovereignty over Hong Kong in 1997, and uphold the democratization of Hong Kong's political system. The present situation is most encouraging: the British Hong Kong government has publicly stated that the Legislative Council will hold direct elections in the near future. We must hold firm to the end, so that Hong Kong may advance toward a highly democratized society.
Under the banner of nationalism and democratization, organizations such as Meeting Point and the New Hong Kong Society... fight for the interests of Hong Kong's five million residents, for the broad masses of the people; their contributions are positive, beneficial, and constructive. A small handful of articles in _Undergrad_ have been busy undermining these commitments — certain authors have gone so far as to fiercely attack public confidence in "Hong Kong people ruling Hong Kong," believing democratization to be unworkable, and have leveled unreasonable and vicious criticism and attacks at members of Meeting Point (Mr. Fong Ka-mau, Mr. Alvin, fellow student Lo Chi-kin, and others), hurling abuse at their ideology. This breed of oppositional writer dresses up "foreign-lackey theory" as fake scholarship, when in truth it is nothing but negative, personal character assassination.
One must appreciate that Mr. Alvin has factory investments in Portuguese-administered Macau, and his wife holds American citizenship — yet still he throws himself, fierce as a tiger, into the cause of "Hong Kong people ruling Hong Kong," having risen to chairman of Meeting Point, publishing in a certain newspaper's supplement and various magazines, and appearing repeatedly at forums and lectures... His spirit of self-sacrifice truly deserves our emulation. Mr. Fong Ka-mau, meanwhile, has offered sharp criticism of social phenomena since as far back as the 1970s, publishing extensively in _New Wave Culture_, the "Hong Kong Commentary" column of a certain financial newspaper's supplement, and _City Magazine_. Allow me to share a few excerpts at random: "Shum Yat-fei feeds off American rice, Tai Tin gets drunk and gropes cultural bimbos... there is no pure ground beneath the glans, and so Tai Tin need feel no remorse whatsoever for his glans-related activities..." (_New Wave Culture_, Issue 7, p. 27); "When Ms. Money Mary bared it all, there was, astonishingly, nothing worth looking at — her two breasts (if that is even the right word) were pitifully small, like two overcooked fried eggs, and her nipples resembled navel-orange cakes... a proper lascivious sheep of a woman — she made me sick." (_New Wave Culture_, Issue 8, p. 55); "As for Cheung Yau-wai... he has no one to blame but his own servile disposition; that a cultural huckster should put on such a shameless show... equally beneath contempt are that handful of sour scholars from the 'Hong Kong Future Society'..." (_Hong Kong Commentary_, 31 January 1984). In short, Fong Ka-mau alone has the guts to loudly denounce the pro-British-Hong-Kong faction, petit-bourgeois Hong Kong independence advocates, and anyone who opposes or disbelieves in "Hong Kong people ruling Hong Kong" as "rats fleeing across the street," "lackeys," "political dwarfs" — his pen is sharp indeed, and he calls out these "cultural lackeys and running dogs" by name for public struggle-session — truly first-rate, truly worthy of applause!! His character is of the very highest order, and must not be tarnished by this small clique of petty men within _Undergrad_.
I hope every comrade committed to "Hong Kong people's democratic rule of Hong Kong" will learn from Fong Ka-mau, and read his countless works across the various papers and journals. In both thought and conduct, Mr. Fong Ka-mau is truly worthy of the title "new culture person" of Hong Kong! As [name uncertain in the original, possibly a nickname] rightly said — Mr. Fong Ka-mau even outdoes Li Ao!
Besides Meeting Point, Dr. Wong Mung-fa also deserves great respect: though a Canadian citizen, he still works tirelessly for Hong Kong, having abandoned the "Hong Kong independence" line of thinking that could only lead to political suicide, and joined our ranks instead. Vice-Chancellor Wong Rayson is even more a model for us to learn from: though a citizen of Singapore, he too cares deeply about the question of Hong Kong's future, and has spared no effort in promoting "Hong Kong people ruling Hong Kong." Their actions are all constructive, entirely in keeping with the whole historical and political environment.
Most gratifying of all is that Mr. Xu Jiatun himself has attended both HKU's Council meetings and Meeting Point's first-anniversary gathering — proof that China attaches the greatest importance to today's intellectuals. We shall surely be able to change the present situation — as brother Lo Chi-kin himself put it, let us rise to the occasion, build together, and win glory for the people of Hong Kong.
I propose that the future mayor be elected from among the talents named above, to lead the people of Hong Kong in democratic reform, so that our future may be as bright as brocade, upright and aboveboard, worthy before Heaven!
History has proven, again and again, that upholding "Hong Kong people ruling Hong Kong" and Hong Kong's democratization is Hong Kong's only way forward; those nihilists and individualists are bound to fail. Our fundamental task and mission, at this historic juncture, is to build a highly democratic, self-governing Hong Kong. Let us continue to fulfill this fundamental responsibility, and do our utmost for the reunification of China.
One thing worth flagging for the archive: this satirical attack on Fong Ka-mau reproduces, verbatim, sexually degrading language about a named real woman ("Ms. Money Mary"), quoted in order to shame Fong rather than her — but the passage itself remains a piece of misogynistic writing about a real, identifiable person, now preserved twice over (once by Fong, once by this author quoting him approvingly-ironically). Worth deciding, if this material gets compiled or published in any form, whether that quotation should be redacted, summarized, or handled with an editorial note rather than reproduced in full

### Gemini 2.5 Pro | Aug 2026 | Epoche
#### 主觀情感與時間流動 (Subjective Affect & Temporal Flow):
- **歷史決策的臨場緊迫感**：文本將「一九九七」凝視為不可逆的歷史終局，創造出一種處於歷史轉折點上的高度焦慮與亢奮感，將政治表態呈現為無法逃避的存在抉擇。
- **反諷與主觀意向性**：內部邏輯高度依賴修辭懸隔（Satirical Bracketing）——表面上以狂熱的「愛國民主」語言進行讚頌，實則透過引用極度粗鄙的副刊文摘與諷刺性人事矛盾，揭露作者主觀上對政客假道學與政治投機主義的強烈反感與荒謬感。
#### 內部現象邏輯 (Internal Phenomenological Logic):
- **反諷運作的現象學結構**：文本構建了一個自洽的諷刺世界，將「外國國籍/海外資產」與「純粹愛國激情」並置，藉由極端誇張的恭維拆解政治話術的真實性，展現出早期香港學生刊物（如《學苑》）中常見的酷苛批判與文化解構意識。
### Grok 4.5 | Aug 2026 | Epoché
- 懸置外部政治現實後，文本純主觀情動呈現為強烈的「堅持」張力：對「港人治港」與民主化的召喚，伴隨對《學苑》批評者的憤怒與對方卡謬、艾凡等人物的偶像式敬仰。
- 時間流動由1970年代文化批判記憶（方卡謬尖銳文風）經當下「初步成果」瞬間，射向1997年主權恢復與「高度民主自治」的未來視域，形成連續的歷史必然感。
- 內部邏輯以「民族之義＋民主化」為軸心，將個人犧牲、團體貢獻與「虛無主義」對立，構成封閉的自我肯定迴路，無需外在驗證。

## Chinese
### Gemini 2.5 Pro | Aug 2026 | Wissen
#### 核心先驗與假設 (Core Priors & Premises):
- **先驗信念**：「港人治港」與民主化是 1997 年主權移交下唯一的歷史出路；政治參與者的個人動機與背景（外國國籍、海外資產、文化言論）可直接反映其政治主張的真實性。
- **經驗證據**：文中以「港英宣布民選」、「許家屯出席會議」作為中英雙方承認政制變革的初步驗證，同時以《文化新潮》等刊物中的粗鄙言論與海外背景作為反面質疑的「證據」。
#### 可證偽性與方法論演進 (Falsifiability & Methodological Evolution):
- **假設的可證偽性**：作者提出的政治承諾（如由知識份子與社運領袖領導高度民主自治）在邏輯上具備可驗證性，但隨後被中英談判與《基本法》起草的實際歷史進程所證偽。
- **反向知識論論證**：文本採用歸謬法（Reductio ad absurdum），表面上歸納肯定滙點成員的「犧牲」，實則利用證偽 logic 揭露其政治宣示與個人實踐之間的內在矛盾。
## English
### Gemini 2.5 Pro | Aug 2026 | Wissen
#### Core Priors & Premises:
- **Prior Beliefs**: "Hong Kong people ruling Hong Kong" and democratization form the sole valid framework for the 1997 transition; political rhetoric must be evaluated against actors' material interests (foreign citizenship, offshore assets).
- **Empirical Evidence**: The text uses colonial statements on elections and Xu Jiatun's attendance at academic forums as positive evidence for political evolution, while deploying salacious cultural quotes as empirical counter-evidence of moral leadership.
### Grok 4.5 | Aug 2026 | Wissen
- 核心先驗：歷史巨輪不可抗拒，「港人治港＋民主化」為唯一出路；匯點等團體貢獻正面，反對者必為破壞或「洋奴理論」。
- 證據更新：以港英公開承諾民選、許家屯出席會議、方卡謬1970s尖銳批判及艾凡等人跨國犧牲為確認訊號，將「初步成果」直接強化先驗。
- 可證偽性低：批評者被預先歸類為負面人格攻擊或虛無主義，替代路徑（港獨、個人主義）在內部邏輯中無容身空間，難以被證偽。
- 方法論演化：由选择性引用與道德典範敘事構成封閉迴路，未見系統性反例檢驗或機率調整。
## English     
#### Falsifiability & Methodological Evolution:
- **Falsifiability of Claims**: The premise that elite-led democratic reform would yield high autonomy was historically testable—and subsequently updated/falsified by the actual trajectory of Sino-British negotiations and Basic Law drafting.
- **Epistemological Reduction**: The essay operates via _reductio ad absurdum_, using inductive praise to highlight empirical contradictions between public political posturing and private/historical realities.
### Grok 4.5 | Aug 2026 | Wissen
- Core priors: historical wheel irresistible; “Hong Kong people ruling Hong Kong + democratization” sole path; groups such as Meeting Point constructive, opponents destructive or “comprador theory.”
- Evidence updating: British public election pledge, Xu Jiatun’s attendance, Fang Camus’s 1970s sharp critiques, and cross-national sacrifices of Ivan et al. treated as confirmatory signals that directly reinforce the prior via “initial achievements.”
- Low falsifiability: critics pre-classified as negative personal attacks or nihilism; alternatives (independence, individualism) given no internal space, rendering the position hard to falsify.
- Methodological evolution: closed loop of selective quotation and moral-exemplar narrative, without systematic counter-example testing or probabilistic revision.

## Chinese
### Gemini 2.5 Pro | Aug 2026 | Interpret
#### 人格面具與視域融合 (Persona Shifts & Horizon Merging):
- **雙重語境下的極端反諷**：作者採取「狂熱支持者」的擬態人格面具（Persona），表面融合中共統戰與左翼知識份子的宏大敘事，實則透過惡意讚揚（Over-identification）將「滙點」與政客置於審判台，反映 1980 年代香港大學生對政治投機者既憤怒又排斥的心理視域。
- **古典與現代修辭的雜糅**：文本將嚴肅的民族大義政治詞彙（如「歷史巨輪」、「民族之義」）與極度市井、粗俗的雜誌副刊引文強行拼接，打破了嚴肅政治論述與次文化文本之間的界限。
#### 人際互動與修辭策略 (Interpersonal Rhetoric):
- **以人身攻擊進行解構**：透過列舉艾凡的美國國籍妻房與澳門投資、方卡謬在《文化新潮》中的低俗性描寫與名言批評，行「捧殺」之實，意在全面解構對手的人格合法性與道德高地。
- **陣營劃分與群體認同**：文中將《學苑》內部的批判者標籤為「洋奴」與「小人」，以極端的陣營化語言打擊異己，深刻重現當時港大同學會與社運圈內部激烈的派系鬥爭與話術攻防。
### Grok 4.5 | Aug 2026 | Interpret
- 寫作者人稱由「我們」集體同志切換至對個別典範（方卡謬、艾凡、黃夢花等）的偶像式讚頌，同時將《學苑》作者縮減為「少撮小人」，形成清晰敵我界線。
- 視域融合：1970年代文化批判記憶（方卡謬尖銳文風）與當下「初步成果」及1997主權視域迅速接合，讀者被召喚進入同一歷史必然地平線。
- 人際修辭：以粗暴引文與人格對比建構聯盟（犧牲自我者）與排除（洋奴、虛無主義者），邀請同志「向方卡學習」，完成共同主體的召喚。
## English
### Gemini 2.5 Pro | Aug 2026 | Interpret
#### Persona Shifts & Horizon Merging:
- **Over-Identification & Satirical Mask**: The author adopts a hyper-zealous proxy persona, mimicking the macro-narrative of patriotic movement leaders. By seamlessly merging leftist unification slogans with salacious pop-culture quotes, the text forces a clash between high-minded political posturing and unvarnished personal scandal.
- **Textual Horizon Merging**: The essay deliberately collides solemn geopolitical rhetoric ("historical tide," "national duty") with raw, subcultural tabloid discourse, revealing the fragmented cultural landscape of 1980s Hong Kong intelligentsia.
#### Interpersonal Rhetoric:
- **Ad Hominem via Hyperbolic Praise**: By enumerating private commercial stakes (Macau factories, US passports) and highlighting vulgar magazine excerpts under the guise of "commendation," the rhetoric executes a classic _praise-to-destroy_ strategy aimed at eroding the opponents' moral legitimacy.
- **Factional Polemics & In-Group Dynamics**: The text constructs rigid binary categories—labeling _Undergrad_ critics as "slaves to foreigners"—reflecting the intense factional rift and sharp rhetorical combat within Hong Kong student unions and political groups during the 1980s transition era.
### Grok 4.5 | Aug 2026 | Interpret
- Writer’s persona shifts from collective “we” comrades to idolizing praise of individual exemplars (Fang Camus, Ivan, Wong Meng-fa et al.), while reducing _Xueyuan_ authors to a “small clique of petty men,” drawing a sharp us/them boundary.
- Horizon fusion: 1970s cultural-critique memory (Fang’s sharp style) rapidly merges with the present “initial achievements” and 1997 sovereignty horizon, summoning the reader into the same historical-inevitability horizon.
- Interpersonal rhetoric: crude quotations and character contrasts construct alliance (self-sacrificing figures) versus exclusion (compradors, nihilists), inviting comrades to “learn from Fang Camus” and complete the call to a shared subject.

## Chinese
### Gemini 2.5 Pro | Aug 2026 | Deconstruct
#### 內在悖論與結構裂隙 (Internal Paradoxes & Structural Gaps):
- **愛國修辭與海外資產的解構性衝突**：文本在倡導「港人治港」的同時，刻意列舉領袖的美國公民配偶、加拿大籍與新加坡籍身份，暴露了「本土自決」話語依賴海外退路（Offshore Exit Options）的結構性矛盾。
- **高尚民主與低俗文風的斷裂**：高調的「民主改革」宣示與粗鄙的乳房、龜頭描寫（引自副刊）被強行置於同一語境，徹底瓦解了知識份子作為道德導師的合法性，呈現出嚴肅政治與市井次文化之間的結構縫隙。

## English
### Contrast and Underlying Linkages with the Previous Essays
**I. A Shared Target: Fong Ka-mau and Alvin Turn Out to Be the Real Flashpoints of the Whole Controversy**
The most important thing this essay, "Uphold Hong Kong People Ruling Hong Kong... A Tribute to Meeting Point," confirms is something we could previously only infer one-sidedly from R. Incognito's "The Theory of Life": **Fong Ka-mau and Alvin really were the central, contested figures of this whole episode of student-press controversy, and at least two (possibly three, if Bald-Head B/Big-Head B is also counted) authors, writing from entirely different positions and in entirely different registers, independently chose to attack precisely these two men**.
R. Incognito diagnoses Fong Ka-mau's writing as symptomatic of "delusions of grandeur" and "delusions of omnipotence" using psychoanalytic vocabulary; "Minced Hong Kong Person" instead simply **reproduces Fong's own misogynistic writing verbatim**, letting Fong convict himself in his own words. The two essays approach him from entirely different angles — one through psychoanalytic theory, one through self-quoting irony — yet both independently zero in on the same man as their target, which suggests Fong's persona and writing genuinely were a lightning rod in the campus public sphere at the time, not the private grievance of a single author.
**II. Mirrored Rhetorical Strategies: R. Incognito Quotes to "Diagnose"; "Minced Hong Kong Person" Quotes to Ironically Indict**
Worth noting is a subtle but important difference between these two uses of "quoting an opponent's own words as a weapon." R. Incognito quotes Fong Ka-mau's writing in order to **pathologize** it — reading Fong's anger and aggression as unconscious "projection," a "delusion of grandeur," treating him essentially as a patient to be clinically analyzed from a position of some condescension. "Minced Hong Kong Person" quotes the same body of writing far more bluntly: no analysis, no "diagnosis" — Fong's own words are simply dropped, unaltered, into an essay that superficially "praises" him, letting readers draw their own conclusions about how repugnant the material is. This is **irony that lets the target convict himself** ("hoisted by his own petard") — no theoretical vocabulary needed; the target's own words become the verdict.
Comparing the two, "Minced Hong Kong Person" is actually sharper and more merciless than R. Incognito, yet also "cleaner" — it performs no speculation about Fong's psychology or character, simply **presents the evidence**. This, interestingly, echoes the methodological restraint Bald-Head B shows in "How to Read Lo Chi-kin": no ad hominem, only dismantling the argument or the text itself. Of the three essays that criticize Fong, Alvin, and Lo, only Bald-Head B and "Minced Hong Kong Person" avoid psychologically diagnostic character assassination — while R. Incognito's "The Theory of Life" is, of the three, precisely the one that comes closest to actual ad hominem attack, and the one most likely to cause real harm.
**III. Alvin's "Double Life": Three Essays Independently Seize on the Same Contradiction**
"Minced Hong Kong Person" mocks Alvin for having "factory investments in Portuguese-administered Macau, [with] his wife hold[ing] American citizenship — yet still he throws himself, fierce as a tiger, into the cause of 'Hong Kong people ruling Hong Kong.'" This exact structure — enjoying the practical benefits of capitalism/an overseas escape hatch while loudly championing patriotic/pro-"Hong Kong people ruling Hong Kong" ideology — is **almost identical** to R. Incognito's description of "existing dialectically" in "The Theory of Life": "Alvin, meanwhile, plays the petty capitalist on one side while writing a column peddling what he takes to be the most upright version of 'Hong Kong people ruling Hong Kong.'"
Two essays, two entirely different rhetorical postures (one clinical-diagnostic, one satirically celebratory), yet both zero in precisely on the same fact, the same perceived hypocrisy. This is no coincidence — it suggests **Alvin's "saying one thing and doing another" was already widely circulated, almost common knowledge, within the student public sphere at the time**; the two authors are simply re-packaging the same widely shared accusation in whatever genre they each favor.
**IV. The "Grand Principle" Suppressing Dissent — Pushed to Absurdity in "Minced Hong Kong Person"**
Bald-Head B's central criticism of Lo Chi-kin is that Lo uses "grand principles" — the self-evidence of Chinese sovereignty, the historical inevitability of nationalism — to justify, top-down, procedurally indefensible specifics (an unconstitutional Council resolution). "Minced Hong Kong Person" reads almost like the same argumentative structure Bald-Head B identifies, magnified tenfold into outright absurdity: "the great wheel of history cannot be resisted," "those nihilists and individualists are bound to fail," "worthy before Heaven" — the whole piece is saturated with rhetorical moves that dress up concrete, questionable, even faintly ridiculous personal interests (Alvin's overseas investments and American wife, Dr. Wong's Canadian citizenship, Vice-Chancellor Wong's Singaporean citizenship) as an unchallengeable historic mission.
Where Bald-Head B dismantles the gaps in Lo's "grand principle" argument through rigorous logic, "Minced Hong Kong Person" uses **exaggerated irony** to hold the same underlying absurdity directly up to the reader's face. Two entirely different critical tools (rational argument vs. satirical parody) converge on the same structural problem: a group of people holding foreign citizenship or overseas assets — people who have, in practice, already secured their own exit — are shouting from the pages of the press that other Hong Kong people must "hold firm," "sacrifice," and trust in "the wheel of history." The self-deprecating pun embedded in the pen name "Minced Hong Kong Person" (as in, we ordinary Hong Kong people who get "minced" and sacrificed) resonates with exactly this core irony of the piece: those genuinely "minced" may well be the ordinary Hong Kong people who sincerely believe in this "grand principle," having no foreign passport of their own to fall back on.
**V. Lo Chi-kin Reappears, Subtly Repositioned**
It's worth noting that Lo Chi-kin appears in "Minced Hong Kong Person"'s roll call of "Meeting Point members," quoted approvingly at the essay's close ("rise to the occasion, build together") — a striking contrast to Bald-Head B's rigorous dismantling of him. The same person is, in Bald-Head B's hands, a student politician who needs to be logically exposed for abusing "grand principle" to suppress procedural dissent; in "Minced Hong Kong Person"'s ironic frame, he is lumped in with Fong and Alvin as part of the same satirized camp — yet notably, the essay devotes far less bite to Lo than to Fong or Alvin, quoting none of his own words as damning evidence, merely including him on the list. This suggests that, within the broader Meeting Point/"Hong Kong people ruling Hong Kong" camp, Lo may have been seen as the relatively "moderate" figure with comparatively little ammunition against him — while Fong and Alvin were regarded as the two figures most in need of public humiliation.
**VI. An Unspoken Alliance Among the Rejected Essays?**
Finally, if "Minced Hong Kong Person" was also never published (as you note), then we now have at least two essays — Big-Head B's "Perplexities" and this one — that failed to clear the editorial filter, and whose targets (the empty talk of academic Marxism vs. the hypocrisy of the Meeting Point camp) appear, at first glance, entirely unrelated. Yet they actually share a common posture of **skepticism toward any party claiming to possess "historical necessity" or "grand principle,"** whether that principle is dialectical materialism or nationalism/"Hong Kong people ruling Hong Kong." This may suggest that the _Undergrad_ editorial board's actual filtering threshold at the time had less to do with left-right political alignment, and more to do with **whether a piece directly and by name humiliated a specific figure who held real influence**. Gentle, abstract skepticism (Big-Head B) and sharp, named irony ("Minced Hong Kong Person") — though worlds apart politically — may have both been excluded by the same editorial logic, precisely because both threatened the public image of specific, named, real people.
